review_text:
Where do I even start? 😂

First of all, I have NO idea why it took me so long to finally play this game. It literally sat in my library collecting digital dust for a couple of YEARS, and for some reason, I never bothered to give it a proper shot.

Then one day, I finally decided to fire it up. Now, I'm a huge fan of open-world RPGs, so you'd think I'd be hooked immediately, right? WRONG. 😂

At first, the game felt a little weird. The mechanics were overwhelming, there was so much going on, and although I played for a bit, nothing really clicked. Looking back, I probably just wasn't giving it the attention it deserved.

Fast-forward about a year. I had just finished Tiny Tina's Wonderlands and decided, "You know what? Let's give this thing another chance."

BOY, WAS I IN FOR A RIDE. 🤯

This time, I actually took the time to learn the mechanics, understand the systems, and really dive into everything the game had to offer. And before I knew it, I was completely HOOKED.

Seriously, this game feels like someone took a shopping list of everything I love about video games and said, "Yeah, let's just throw ALL of that in there."

FPS combat? CHECK. ✅

Quests, loot, rewards, and upgrades? CHECK. ✅

Character customization? CHECK. ✅

Driving, car chases, and racing? CHECK. ✅

Hacking, different storylines, exploration, and a ridiculous amount of things to do? CHECK, CHECK, CHECK! ✅

It's honestly insane how much this game has to offer once you really get into it.

Anyway, I guess what I'm trying to say is that I've sunk an absolutely ridiculous number of hours into this game, and somehow, I'm STILL having a blast. Every time I think I'm done, I find another reason to keep playing.

And now, with 2.5 right around the corner?

Are you kidding me?! It's like Christmas came early! 🎁🔥

To think I almost let this gem sit in my library forever. Better late than never, I guess! 😂🎮

review_text:
Absolutely amazing game. Released originally in 2020 to poor reception, but CD Project Red have completely turned the game around. Story is great, missions are great, the world-building is stellar, characters have a *ton* of lore and backstory (you have to find this out through playing sidequests and interacting with the world- the game doesn't like to hold your hand).

Fully open world, mod support, tons of customization with how the class + weapons + crafting system is setup, infinite replayability, and the developers *still* support the game 6 years after release.

Oh, did I mention graphics? They are great; even running on low end, mid range, and high end PCs! There are options to turn on Ray Tracing as well- and those options seem to run great on an RTX 4080 super + Ryzen 9 5950x + 128gb of RAM.

I have completed the main story 3 times, and around 80% of the side quests- and every time I play I find something different to try or interact with; Especially with how many updates they push between each time I have enough time to play the game.

P.S. There is a "Cyberpunk Edgerunners" show- highly recommend to watch that in addition to playing the game. Season 2 just dropped 2026/10/20. Apparently Cyberpunk 2 is confirmed to be in development, so it seems the Cyberpunk franchise will continue on!

review_text:
I've immensely enjoyed my experience of Cyberpunk 2077 as a new denizen of Night City. 

The main story is fantastic, filled with engaging characters and dialogue choices that matter. Keanu is of course a highlight as the charismatic rockerboy Johnny Silverhand, but many others shine. The soundtrack and voice acting is stellar and supports scenes and brings to life this ridiculous feudal-corporate-run-cyber-futurist-netrunner setting so much so that it really feels alive as you move through it on your quest striving for the big leagues... It's easily one of my favourite games now and is night and day from how it was released. 

CD Red have added a lot of free content and a fantastic DLC over the game's lifespan to date for those that want more after the base game and fixed the vast majority of bugs and quality of life issues. We're up to 2.5 now as of 22.10.26!

There's a significant multitude of weapons and cyberware abilities, consumables and other gear; combined with expansive perk trees and a skills progression system means there is a ton of possible builds for new playthroughs (or switching up an existing one with a very generous re-allocating system). Also, the movement system with parkour and cyberware upgrades is great, from slow motion to double or charged jumps and dashes. As a result you can traverse most of the city's verticality through creative use of the latter methods in your exploration. Give it a try and see how far you can get without elevators and 'standard routes' to objectives (or just for free roaming exploration). You might find some jobs are made much easier and new routes and shortcuts you wouldn't have otherwise considered open up.

Not to mention the significant amount of side missions and activities you can do. Different fixers across the city offer different jobs that scale in reward and difficulty as your street cred climbs and as you complete them. Everything from heists, assassinations, death races and detective work are up for taking on! Vehicles are varied and interesting, fast travel works via waypoint system as well as the subway/rail system and soon to be added a cab system (Delamain) or auto-driving enabled for your own vehicles so you don't have to lift a finger as you cruise through the neon soaked urban sprawl, or drift into the desert badlands outside the city limits to take in the views and get some cool photo mode shots. 

All in all, you'll have a blast with all you can do. Just don't try to complete too much too quickly or you may burnout or go cyberpsycho. Pace yourself and enjoy it. 

See you at the Afterlife chooms.

review_text:
When playing Cyberpunk 2077 you will find yourself often struggling to place the game in terms of ranking. The city, quests, overall promise of the game and gunplay feels very good and very much like the game is one of the 'grand games'. However, when comparing it to other 'grand games' like Baldur's Gate 3, Red Dead Redemption 2 or Elden Ring, Cyberpunk falls short.

The game thrives in its cinematic aspects. Big flashy gun fight, with smooth gunplay and more quiet scenes with beautiful images of Night City woven into each other create a feeling of playing an action movie. The different weapons and builds also allow for some customisability, which makes finding new weapons always exciting, whilst the voice acting and music strengthen this feeling even more allowing you to really immerse yourself in Night City. Moreover, the aspect which I found the best in this game was the design of Night City and the theme of the story. Whilst on the surface the story mainly revolves around "becoming a legend" and eventually other things (no spoilers), underneath the entire game heavily showcases how class-difference becomes more enhanced by technology and seems like a dystopian warning for the future. The city with its outrageous ads, dirty streets and high skyscrapers perfectly encapsulates this feeling as you drive through it between quests.

However, this game does have its downsides. Mainly in the details of immersion. Most NPCs, with which you interact feel rather lifeless (besides the main ones relevant for cutscenes and in story missions), in addition many spaces in the game, especially in the city feel rather empty. My original thought on how to approach this game was that I would (much like in a real city) try to get lost in the city and discover it. but besides the locations for vendors and tarot cards indicated on the map most of these efforts didn't really lead to anything. A lot of the things you can do (romance, have your own apartment, fighting) feels like a side-idea. This means that originally your first thought might be: "OMG I CAN DO ALL OF THIS????", but after actually buying an apartment you will figure out that it can do very little and is a bit of a clickbait scenario. 

Overall, I would recommend this game to anybody with a device able to run all the cool graphics, who likes cinematic games with loads of guns and a dystopian underlying theme. review_text:
Spoilers (duh)
I purchased Cyberpunk 2077 in December of 2025 & have only just finished my first playthrough so I'm here to talk that along side Edgerunners Seasons 1 & 2.
Before watching Edgerunners 1 I purchased & started to play 2077 because it was 65% off at the time so I figured why not. I picked the Corpo start & made my way to Dex at which point I stopped & moved on to other games but never ended up going back. I tried a 2nd time after watching Edgerunners 1 with a bit of a sour taste as I was not a fan of season 1 due to the writing dessions but I'm not about to go into that as it wasn't the games fault. This time only making it to meet Jackie in Lizzies before putting it back down & not playing it again.
It took watching Edgerunners 2 to actually spark a want to play 2077 as I believe season 2 shined an interesting light on Night City. Picking 2077 back up this last week I eneded up putting about 40hours into the main mission & a handful of the side missions.
Female V, Corpo Start, focusing stats on Reflex & Technically Ability, once I gotten Air Dash. I put it into Intelligence & a bit more technically ability.

Playing the game it's very clear I have a major skill issue when it comes to driving as it felt like I couldn't keep control of most cars. Without a dedicated handbrake button every turn became an uncontrolable drift & therefore once I could I took up dashing & airdashing everywhere which was the right call to make as there was a plentful amount of roofs & highways/roads to jump between making my travels quicker than car would have been. 

The story so far as well has been great. The path I lead brought me to following Takemura & eventually trusting him after kidnapping Hanako & bringing her to Yorinobu in return for Arasaka to remove Johnny. Yes this does mean I choice to not let Johnny take over in the end but, I did still bring Johnny to Rogue for their Date & did 1 last gig with the Samurai as playing as V. It only felt right after he saved my life (twice) even tho I did have to 2nd thoughts after the 1st time I let him take control to meet with Rogue & had the wildest night. I did still promise to Flatline/Zero out Adam Smasher & I did & said my goodbyes the best I could but he didn't like me (us?) every much after taking the pill on Misty's roof. 

The game isn't without its flaws still. I would never have brought 2077 full price after seeing the release state but it has clearly been improved massively. In saying that here's a list of a some flaws still;
- Driving
See above
- Customisation options
For how many options you get for designing your face & body it doesn't feel like that was foillowed up with the clothing options available in-game. During downtime either waiting for messages to follow up on missions or not wanting to do other missions just yet I found myself checking out all the clothing shops & what was available didn't really feel like something I wanted to even consider as it was tacky or about 4 different recolours.
- Mini-map Task routing
The routing didn't seem to account for the fact I wasn't in a vichle & therefore didn't use any alleyways or sidwalks that I could see & was infact quicker than following the road. There was also a situation where the route just lead to a building & stopped, I went to the building even tho I knew I need to continue further to see what would happen & then it updated with the rest of the route.
- Not being able to pause/save.
Life happens & during some cutsenses you can't open the pause menu which means you can't save the game & come back it to. so while I have 48hours ingame my saves say I've only spent 35hours in it which leaves the rest of this time just having the game opened & 'paused' in the background on the Character menu.
- Looting
Sometimes (mostly with robots) it was impossible to loot them despite showing available loot as I couldn't find a way to access the drops.
- Random Menus appearing
Mostly against some walls a small menu will appear which usually meant there's option I can do but looking back over to find it was a very tiny small spot my cursor had to be on & it was an empty box with nothing there.

Despite these negatives and a few more I'm not going to mention cause they were minor ones I'd still recommend 2077 to most people as the story & gameplay is amazing. I do recommend having a beefy PC however, as with my specs running high-ultra settings would get me 60fps max & I wouldn't want to see this game anything visually lower just to keep the FPS as it is so beautful when you can run High-Ultra settings.

I'm about to start my 2nd playthrough as Male V, Streetkid start & given the chance Imma be raiding Arasaka as Johnny this time round🔥

I can't stop playing this masterpiece. I got the game for free on Epic Games store back in 2023. I got passed the gig where you save Sandra Dorsett from the scavs, then mistakenly put the game down and forgot about it for THREE YEARS. My friend came over one day and asked "Hey bro have you seen Cyberpunk Edgerunners?" and from that day on I was obsessed. 

After binging the anime, processing trauma, and fiending for more cyberpunk, I redownloaded the game on Epic. I put in 70 hours into my first playthrough, then decided to buy the ultimate edition here on Steam to continue my playthrough. After Phantom Liberty, this game is literally in the top 3 gaming experiences I've ever had. The soundtrack is absolute peak, and the world never gets boring!

The modding community for this game is amazing as well. Clothes, vehicles, new quests, new cyberware, weapons, and so much more! I've gone crazy with modding this game!
I was so hyped when update 2.5 was announced it brought console mod support and some amazing new content for edgerunners season 2! CDPR still showing love for a 6 year old game by adding many community requested features gives me high hopes for the future of cyberpunk and the future of gaming!

As of writing this review I'm on my third playthrough, still discovering new things, choosing new dialogue I haven't heard, and trying out every build I can think of combining cyberware, attributes and the countless amount of guns. Hunting for Iconics and doing every gig in a different way has become my favorite thing to do early game! It's just insane how replayable this game is! The atmosphere and open world is also the most addictive to explore out of any game I've played! Cyberpunk 2077 had a rough launch, but the people over at CD PROJEKT RED have more than made up for it, and the community is very thankful!

What an insane experience.

This game is far, FAR deeper than I thought it would get. You just play and it keeps on giving you more like a  chest loaded full with springs. The length of the credit list... So many people, an ungodly amount of hours put into making this one title possible.

I don't know how buggy this game was when it first came out. But I do know damn well this game is a near-perfect game. Maybe it's my tendency to love science-fiction. By the way, this game is loaded to the top with nods and references to other sci-fi titles. They're impossible to miss if you know them.

Performance wise the lowest I saw was 50-fps during populated city areas, but that's no big deal. Don't let performance be the roadblock of this experience if your computer is like mine. The game's optimization is still very good.

I can't get over how many memorable characters are there in this game. Holy shit I wanna say so much about this game and I can't find the words for it. Euphoric, fun, amazing. Some parts still maybe buggy, some things are still rough, true, but that didn't get in the way of creating such a grand, long but not necessarily dragging experience. If you see this on sale like I did. BUY IT. You WILL not regret it. Just give this game a fair shot.

I kind of want to delete this game to move onto the Tomb Raider trilogy but I really don't want to. Holy shit man. I love sci-fi, I love Cyberpunk. This game will forever take a place in my heart.

Cyberpunk 2077 is easily one of my favorite games, and it's a game I always find myself coming back to. Night City is an incredible world to explore, filled with detail, atmosphere, and countless things to discover. The story, characters, soundtrack, and overall world-building make for an experience that is hard to forget.

One of the biggest strengths of the game is how immersive it feels. Whether I'm progressing through the main story, exploring the city, taking on side missions, or simply driving around Night City, there's always something that keeps me coming back. The characters are memorable, the story is engaging, and the world feels alive.

While there are still a few minor issues here and there, they don't take away from what makes this game so special. Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those rare games that I can revisit time and time again without getting tired of it.

Pros:

Incredible world-building and atmosphere
Engaging story with memorable characters
Beautiful visuals and attention to detail
Excellent soundtrack
Tons of exploration and replayability
Immersive open world

Cons:

Some minor bugs and glitches
A few activities can become repetitive
Not every side activity feels equally rewarding

Final Verdict: One of my all-time favorite games. Night City is a world I never get tired of returning to, and Cyberpunk 2077 is an experience I'd recommend to just about anyone.

review_text:
# Cyberpunk 2077 — A Game You Have to Learn How to Play

I’ve now put around 160 hours into Cyberpunk 2077, and I think I’m finally getting to grips with what makes this game so special.

I initially played it alongside STALKER 2, which probably wasn’t the best idea. They’re very different games, and I found myself approaching them with the wrong mindset. After taking a break and returning to Cyberpunk, I decided to take my time, learn the systems and develop my character properly.

That made a huge difference.

For me, **Cyberpunk 2077 is a game you have to learn how to play.** Give it time, understand the systems and find a build that suits you. Once things start to click, it becomes a brilliant and incredibly immersive experience.

## Character Progression and Gameplay

I’m very much an RPG player. I like levelling up, improving my character and getting the best equipment and cyberware available before pushing too far into the story.

I’m currently running a Netrunner build with Tier 5++ cyberware. Getting there hasn’t necessarily taken a long time, but there’s certainly a lot to learn.

Working out which cyberdecks to use, which quickhacks to install and how to combine everything effectively involves trial and error. You either need to research the systems or learn by doing. I’ve done a bit of both.

One thing I hadn’t realised initially was just how much of the environment you can interact with. Access Points, terminals, antennae, wall sockets and other devices can be scanned and hacked.

Access Points use Breach Protocol and can reward you with money, quickhack components and sometimes new quickhacks or crafting specs.

Once you start understanding how quickhacks work together, the gameplay becomes much more interesting. If I’m driving and get into combat, I no longer bother trying to take on everyone shooting at me. I’ll simply use a quickhack to blow up their vehicle. Problem solved.

Stealth is another area where the game really opens up. And then there’s Ping: scanning a building, identifying enemies, accessing cameras and systematically taking out targets without ever physically entering the building is incredibly satisfying.

This is where Cyberpunk really shines for me. It’s not just about better weapons or more powerful cyberware. It’s about understanding the tools available and finding creative ways to use them.

## Phantom Liberty

I initially resisted starting Phantom Liberty. I wanted to concentrate on the main game and build my character before adding another major storyline.

I’ve since started playing the expansion alongside the main game, and I’m enjoying that approach. It gives me more to do while developing my character, without feeling that I have to rush either story.

My mission progress probably doesn’t reflect the number of hours I’ve played. I’m quite happy levelling up, improving my build and exploring before moving the story forward.

## V, Johnny Silverhand and the Characters

I’m playing female V, and while I’m enjoying the character, the voice isn’t quite to my taste. That’s entirely subjective, of course. I’d have preferred something more like Lara Croft or Sigourney Weaver in *Alien* and *Aliens*—a stronger, more confident delivery.

Johnny Silverhand was another character I wasn’t entirely sure about at first. I’m a fan of Bill & Ted and Keanu Reeves, but I wondered whether he might become a little overpowering.

I’ve come around to him. I get it now, and he hasn’t been as intrusive as I initially expected.

There’s a lot of dialogue in Cyberpunk, and I’ve learned to slow down and engage with it rather than rushing through. That’s part of playing an RPG, and it makes the characters and story more rewarding.

## Night City and the World

Wow. Night City is something else.

It’s huge, vibrant, visually overwhelming and full of things happening everywhere you look. The neon, lighting and sheer density make it feel like a world of its own.

Having played *The Witcher 3*, it’s fascinating to see how different the two games feel despite coming from the same developer. The Witcher has its own incredible atmosphere, but Night City is much more visually busy and intense.

There’s so much to take in that I’m still discovering things after 160 hours.

## Graphics and Performance

On my system, Cyberpunk 2077 looks fantastic and runs beautifully.

With DLSS enabled, I’m getting around 100 FPS, and the game feels buttery smooth. I’m not experiencing the stuttering or lag that would take me out of the experience.

The RTX 4070 Ti SUPER is an amazing card. Love it.

## Technical Issues

I’ve had a few random crashes, mainly while driving. They haven’t been frequent enough to ruin the experience, but they’re worth mentioning.

Overall, performance has been very good on my system.

## Driving and Traffic AI

This is probably my biggest criticism.

I’m a sim racer, so I’m perhaps more sensitive to vehicle handling than some players. I understand Cyberpunk isn’t a driving simulator, but some of the handling still feels strange.

Motorbikes can be particularly odd uphill. Sometimes they seem to lose traction or struggle to climb, even on an off-road bike. Backing off the throttle can occasionally help, which feels counterintuitive.

The NPC traffic AI can also be frustrating. Cars sometimes stop in the middle of the road for no apparent reason, especially when you’re trying to complete a mission.

It doesn’t break the game, but it’s an area I’d like to see improved.

## Immersion and Gameplay

I’ve spent years working in live sound, where you’re constantly listening, watching, making decisions and keeping track of multiple things at once. Gaming gives me a different way to engage that same kind of concentration.

There are moments when I get completely absorbed in a game and find myself in that familiar zone. Cyberpunk is increasingly giving me that feeling.

The combination of character development, exploration, hacking, stealth and story makes it a game I can spend hours in without feeling that I’m simply going through the motions.

## A Shout-Out to the Developers

I want to give credit to CD Projekt Red. Cyberpunk 2077 had a troubled launch, but the developers have continued to work on and improve the game while also having other projects in development.

That deserves recognition. It doesn’t mean the game is beyond criticism, but a great deal of work and care has gone into bringing Cyberpunk to where it is today.

## Overall Verdict

Cyberpunk 2077 has become one of those games that really rewards patience.

I wasn’t sure I was approaching it in the right way at first. Coming back with a different mindset made all the difference.

The world is incredible, the graphics and performance are excellent on my system, and the Netrunner gameplay has become genuinely satisfying as I’ve learned how to use it.

The driving and traffic AI remain my biggest frustrations, and there are occasional crashes, but neither has been enough to spoil the experience.

**My advice? Give it time. Learn how to play it. Then let Night City take you in.**

## A Note on This Review

This review was written with AI assistance, and I want to be clear about what that means.

I’m dyslexic, and while I have plenty to say, putting my thoughts into a clear, structured piece of writing can be difficult. ChatGPT helps me with grammar, flow, structure and fact-checking.

This isn’t a review I asked AI to write for me. The opinions, experiences and observations are mine. I share my thoughts, work through the ideas, correct and refine the draft, and decide what goes into the final review. AI helps me communicate what I mean.

Without that assistance, I probably wouldn’t write reviews at all. For me, this is a positive use of the technology: it helps me share my experiences and contribute something useful to the gaming community.
